sentences.text: Kendall Reyes is a 22-year-old student and part-time barista who became a customer on 2026-08-28 and held checking account ending 6620.

The account received funds from 17 distinct P2P counterparties with no relationship on file, and D. Vasquez received two P2P transfers and was also a recipient in two other mule alerts at this bank this quarter.

The account received 23 P2P credits totaling $14,860.00 from 2026-09-24 through 2026-10-06, including 10 posted credits totaling $6,120.00 funded by 9 distinct cards on the Orbit Digital Goods compromised-card list.
The account sent funds through 8 ATM withdrawals totaling $5,200.00, 3 crypto-exchange purchases totaling $6,900.00, and 2 P2P debits totaling $2,170.00.
A prior rapid-in/out P2P alert covering 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-12 was closed without a SAR on 2026-09-19 after the customer stated that ticket resales explained the transfers.

The customer-supplied explanation stated that ticket resales and payments to ticket sellers in cash or crypto explained the activity, but it does not explain the compromised-card funding identified in the current review.
The reviewed activity occurred from 2026-09-24 through 2026-10-06, with credits posted over 13 days and debits posted over 12 days.
A $480.00 P2P credit funded by card ending 1188 was attempted on 2026-10-02 at 21:47 after fraud operations blocked the card at 21:12, and the transaction was declined.
ATM withdrawals occurred at 3 distinct locations, including Oakland Fruitvale, San Leandro Bancroft, and Oakland Lake Merritt.
Crypto purchases were sent to Coinvault Exchange, and the account was opened and maintained at the bank in Oakland, California.
The activity is inconsistent with expected part-time wages and family support under $1,500 a month because the observed inflow was 9.9 times expected activity.
The fraud referral identified 9 cards on the compromised-card list that funded P2P pushes to account ending 6620, and a related attempted push was declined after fraud blocked the card.
Funds entered through many-to-one P2P transfers from 17 distinct counterparties, with observed pass-through of 96.0% within 48 hours.
Funds were rapidly dispersed through ATM cash withdrawals, crypto-exchange purchases, and P2P transfers, which comprised 100.0% of the observed cash-out channels.

rationale.text: The money mule typology is matched because all 6 of 6 indicators fired, including rapid pass-through, many-to-one transfers, inflow materially above expected activity, fraud-listed funding, new-account activity, and cash-out channels; the activity remains unexplained despite the customer’s ticket-resale explanation.

next_steps: Complete supervisory review and file the SAR by 2026-11-02 if approved.
Preserve transaction, fraud-referral, card-linkage, and counterparty records supporting the suspected money-mule activity.
Coordinate with Fraud Operations regarding the 9 compromised cards and the declined attempted push funded by card ending 1188.

sentences.text: Kendall Reyes is a 22-year-old student and part-time barista who became a customer on 2026-08-28 and held checking account ending 6620.

The account received funds from 17 distinct P2P counterparties with no relationship on file, and D. Vasquez received two P2P transfers and was also a recipient in two other mule alerts at this bank this quarter.

The account received 23 P2P credits totaling $14,860.00 from 2026-09-24 through 2026-10-06, including 10 posted credits totaling $6,120.00 funded by 9 distinct cards on the Orbit Digital Goods compromised-card list.
The account sent funds through 8 ATM withdrawals totaling $5,200.00, 3 crypto-exchange purchases totaling $6,900.00, and 2 P2P debits totaling $2,170.00.
A prior rapid-in/out P2P alert covering 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-12 was closed without a SAR on 2026-09-19 after the customer stated that ticket resales explained the transfers.

The customer-supplied explanation stated that ticket resales and payments to ticket sellers in cash or crypto explained the activity, but it does not explain the compromised-card funding identified in the current review.
The reviewed activity occurred from 2026-09-24 through 2026-10-06, with credits posted over 13 days and debits posted over 12 days.
A $480.00 P2P credit funded by card ending 1188 was attempted on 2026-10-02 at 21:47 after fraud operations blocked the card at 21:12, and the transaction was declined.
ATM withdrawals occurred at 3 distinct locations, including Oakland Fruitvale, San Leandro Bancroft, and Oakland Lake Merritt.
Crypto purchases were sent to Coinvault Exchange, and the account was opened and maintained at the bank in Oakland, California.
The activity is inconsistent with expected part-time wages and family support under $1,500 a month because the observed inflow was 9.9 times expected activity.
The fraud referral identified 9 cards on the compromised-card list that funded P2P pushes to account ending 6620, and a related attempted push was declined after fraud blocked the card.
Funds entered through many-to-one P2P transfers from 17 distinct counterparties, with observed pass-through of 96.0% within 48 hours.
Funds were rapidly dispersed through ATM cash withdrawals, crypto-exchange purchases, and P2P transfers, which comprised 100.0% of the observed cash-out channels.

rationale.text: The money mule typology is matched because all 6 of 6 indicators fired, including rapid pass-through, many-to-one transfers, inflow materially above expected activity, fraud-listed funding, new-account activity, and cash-out channels; the activity remains unexplained despite the customer’s ticket-resale explanation.

Preserve transaction, fraud-referral, card-linkage, and counterparty records supporting the suspected money-mule activity.
Coordinate with Fraud Operations regarding the 9 compromised cards and the declined attempted push funded by card ending 1188.

The activity is inconsistent with expected part-time wages and family support under $1,500 a month because the observed inflow was 9.9 times expected activity.
The fraud referral identified 9 cards on the compromised-card list that funded P2P pushes to account ending 6620, and a related attempted push was declined after fraud blocked the card.
Funds entered through many-to-one P2P transfers from 17 distinct counterparties, with observed pass-through of 96.0% within 48 hours.
Funds were rapidly dispersed through ATM cash withdrawals, crypto-exchange purchases, and P2P transfers, which comprised 100.0% of the observed cash-out channels.

decision.rationale: The money mule typology is matched because all 6 of 6 indicators fired, including rapid pass-through, many-to-one transfers, inflow materially above expected activity, fraud-listed funding, new-account activity, and cash-out channels; the activity remains unexplained despite the customer’s ticket-resale explanation.
